title: Charges and Payments Across Two Sites — Community Rules & Site Care Statement Note
content:
Where a customer holds two Community Rules & Site Care plan records, each record keeps its own statement and its own history:

1. Every notice and every charge belongs to the plan record of the site where the violation occurred.
2. Repeat-violation counts run per site and never across sites.
3. A payment is applied only to the plan record whose statement it names.

A rules balance is never moved to the site-lease ledger, the utility account or the security deposit.

## The same rules, read as questions

**A lawn notice is served at the new site while the old site's lease is still running. Which record carries it?** The record of the new site, because the violation occurred there.

**Does an earlier notice at the old site count toward a repeat at the new site?** No. Repeat-violation counts run per site, so a notice at one site never counts toward the sequence at the other.

**A payment names the old site's statement while the new site's statement also shows a balance. Where is it applied?** Only to the old site's record, the record whose statement it names.

**Can a rules balance be moved onto the site rent ledger, the utility account or the security deposit?** No; a rules balance stays on the rules and site-care statement.

## Hypothetical illustration

A customer holds record A (old site) and record B (new site). A debris notice served at site B, and any charge arising from it, sit on record B. A payment naming record A's statement reduces only record A's balance, whatever record B shows.
